Description: Twenty-three fragments from Cave 4, published in DJD XVII (Cross, Parry and Saley), preserving parts of 1 Samuel only: Samuel's farewell, Saul's reign, the anointing of David (1 Samuel 16), David's flight from Saul, and David at Keilah. Shorter catalogue summaries compress this to 1 Samuel 16:1-11; 19:10-17; 20:27-42; 21:1-10; 23:9-17; the fuller range here follows the DJD-based survey of Samuel and Kings.
Significance: Dated to around 250 BCE, it is among the oldest surviving manuscripts of biblical Hebrew and the earliest of the four Qumran Samuel copies, predating the Batch 1 copy 4Q51 (4QSama, 50-25 BCE) by about two centuries.
